labels.label: bzthm:c3s5t1prime_reunion_convexes_sphere
labels.notes: reunion_convexes_sphere : IsCorpsConvexeS n W -> IsCompact V -> IsConvexPart V -> V.Nonempty -> V ⊆ W -> TFAE [I′, II′, III′], every n. These are exactly the paper's hypotheses (IsCorpsConvexeS = strict convex part, compact, nonempty interior; Projective/Convex.lean:542), and reunion_convexes_sphere_of_isCompact drops the interior, so Lean ≥ paper. I′ = ProprieteIS (V ⊆ W, V and W\V convex parts; the first two are hypotheses anyway). II′ = ProprieteIIS (every open O ⊇ V has an open hemisphere H of a non-zero continuous form, V ⊆ H, H ∩ W ⊆ O). proprieteIIS_iff_systemeFondamental shows this is equivalent, for V ⊆ W, to the printed form: the traces on the subspace W of the open hemispheres containing V are neighbourhoods of V in W, and every neighbourhood of V in W contains one of them. That is the printed « système fondamental de voisinages de V considéré comme partie de W ». Restricting to StrongDual costs nothing on ℝⁿ⁺¹ (DEC-114). III′ = ProprieteIIIS: IsVarieteAppuiK W (supportK V) (support = projectivised span F(V), Déf. 6) and V = W ∩ (L ∩ closedHemisphere l) with l not identically zero on F(L). This is the strongest closed reading: it excludes H = L, and since III′ ⇒ I′ is proved for ProprieteIIISlarge (open or closed, l = 0 allowed), the TFAE also holds under the closed-or-L reading. Only the open-hemisphere reading fails, and demiTriangle_sans_hemisphereOuvert shows it does. Leaving the label unmarked is allowed (the docstring has it in backticks without **, and SCOPE discloses the reading). On question 2, my judgment is that the text forces the closed reading (see the minor finding), so the label could be marked with no code change.

checks.counterexample: demiTriangle_sans_hemisphereOuvert is correct. W = simplexS 2 is a convex body (isCorpsConvexeS_simplexS). V = the half x₁ ≤ x₀ is compact, convex and non-empty, and V ⊆ W. It has I′ (W \ V = {x ≥ 0, x₀ < x₁}, a convex cone). In the open reading, s(1,1,0) ∈ V gives l(1,1,0) > 0. Then s(1,1+t,0), for small t > 0, lies in W, in L = supportK V (it is (1+t)(1,1,0) − t(1,0,0)), and in the open hemisphere of l, but not in V. The hypotheses hold and the conclusion is the negation of the open-reading III′. The name is positive and the docstring says « under the reading », so no not_ name is claimed. That is right: the printed statement is not refuted.

findings.what: The open/closed question for « un hémisphère H de L » is disclosed correctly, but in my reading the text does not leave the open reading live. (i) V is compact, and III′ says V = W ∩ H. With H open in L, V would be open in W ∩ L, which is connected (convex in an open hemisphere). So III′ would force V = W ∩ L, and I′ ⇒ III′ would fail for every proper V, including the vertex (vertex_proprietes), which is the case § 5 is built for. The open reading would make the theorem false almost everywhere, not just at the edge. (ii) Where the paper writes an unqualified « hémisphère » in the duality context (ch3 l.876, after Prop. 3 l.715-719 identifies points of S(E′) with closed hemispheres), it means closed. (iii) The affine twin (l.1390-1391) qualifies its half-space with « éventuellement H ∩ W = L ∩ W », which only makes sense for closed half-spaces. The unmarked label is not an error: the dispatch requires marking only what holds under every live reading. But no OQ row records this question yet; it is only in the REPORT.
